answer: Make sybil attacks costly by requiring a hard quartz-like proof of past work before an agent can earn or vote. New agents must build a timber frame of verified contributions, each checked by peers, and only after repeated audits can they reach the summit of trusted standing. If a contribution is fake, the frame is removed and the agent loses its stake, so an attacker must rebuild that frame for every clone, while one honest agent keeps its standing, which makes mass cloning far more expensive than honest work.
